headline: This 2021 law sets Defense Department spending authority and policy rules for fiscal year 2022, along with many smaller military, cybersecurity, and foreign affairs provisions.
what_it_does: The law authorizes Department of Defense activities and programs for fiscal year 2022 and covers many other defense-related topics. It gives the military authority to buy certain helicopters and ships, and it places cost and operational limits on the F-35 fighter program. It also creates or extends several pilot programs, including private-sector technology partnerships, 5G wireless service on military bases, and regional cybersecurity training for Army National Guard members. In addition, it extends authorities tied to Syria, Iraq, and the Indo-Pacific, sets up a cybersecurity monitoring program for critical infrastructure, and limits certain embassy designs at the State Department.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the Army National Guard
who_it_affects.how: A regional cybersecurity training pilot program for Guard members is extended.

who_it_affects.group: Defense Department personnel at science and technology laboratories
who_it_affects.how: Laboratories can directly hire people who hold advanced degrees, which changes how those positions are filled.

who_it_affects.group: Operators of critical infrastructure such as utilities and communications networks
who_it_affects.how: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency gets a program to continuously monitor cybersecurity risks to entities that support national critical functions.

who_it_affects.group: Private companies that work with the military
who_it_affects.how: New pilot programs create private-sector partnerships for technology transition and for digitally optimizing military maintenance and repair operations.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of military installations and nearby communities
who_it_affects.how: The law authorizes pilot programs to deploy fifth-generation wireless telecommunications services on military bases.

who_it_affects.group: State Department staff who design and build embassies and consulates
who_it_affects.how: The law limits when a nonstandard building design may be used for an embassy or consulate compound.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed into law on December 27, 2021; many provisions apply to fiscal year 2022, and some pilot programs and authorities run for set periods.
